## Pakistani ships arrive with oil at Karachi port

ISLAMABAD: A Pakistani vessel carrying oil arrived at the southern
port city of Karachi after transiting the Strait of Hormuz, while a
second vessel reached the port via a different route, a Karachi Port
Trust spokesperson said on Wednesday. Spokesperson Shariq
Farooqi said more Pakistani-flagged ships are expected this month
to deliver much-needed oil from Gulf countries. The development
comes days after Pakistan said Iran allowed 20 more Pakistani-
flagged ships through the Strait of Hormuz, calling it a
“constructive gesture” to ease tensions.

## Iran clears Bangladesh fuel ships transit

DHAKA: Iran has approved safe passage for six Bangladesh-bound
fuel ships through the Strait of Hormuz, its envoy in Dhaka said. The
vessels — five LNG shipments from Qatar and one crude cargo from
Saudi Arabia — are awaiting transit amid ongoing regional conflict.
Bangladesh, heavily reliant on imports, faces dwindling reserves.
Iran said it aims to prevent hardship. Officials in Dhaka say
confirmation is awaited, but developments appear positive as
disruptions continue to impact vital oil routes. The ships carry nearly
5 lakh tonnes of LNG and about 79,000 tonnes of crude.

## Top Hezbollah commander among
seven killed in Israel’s Beirut strike

BEIRUT

Israel killed a top Hezbollah
commander on Wednesday, two
sources told AFP, in a Beirut
strike that Lebanon’s health
ministry said killed seven
people.

A Lebanese security source
and a Hezbollah source told AFP
that the commander, Youssef
Hashem, had been responsible for
the group’s military affairs in
Iraq and was in a meeting inside
a tent when Israel struck. Israel’s
military said Hashem was Hez-
bollah’s commander for its south
Lebanon front.

Lebanon was drawn into the
West Asia war in early March
when the Tehran-backed Hezbol-
lah launched rockets towards Is-
rael to avenge a US-Israeli attack
that killed Iran’s supreme leader
Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Israel
has responded with massive
strikes across Lebanon and a
ground offensive.

A source close to Hezbollah
said Hashem is “the highest-
ranking official to be targeted
since the start of the war”.

Another Hezbollah member,
Mohammad Baqir al-Nabulsi,
was also killed in the strike on

the Beirut area of Jnah, the
group said.

Israel’s emergency services
said 14 people, including an 11-
year-old girl, were wounded near
Tel Aviv on Wednesday during a
missile attack that the military
blamed on Iran.

Later in the day, medics said
they were treating a 61-year-old
man in mild condition with blast
injuries in the north following
fire from Lebanon, where Israeli
forces are fighting Iran-backed
Hezbollah.

## Houthis claim Israel strike

Yemen’s Houthis claimed a mis-
sile attack against Israel that
they said was launched jointly
with their backer Iran and Leba-
non’s Hezbollah group — the
third such attack by the rebels
since they entered the West Asia
war. Earlier, Israel’s military
said its air defences had re-
sponded to a missile launched
from Yemen, later announcing
that residents were “permitted
to leave protected spaces in all
areas of the country”. AFP

domestic airlines as rates up 100%

THE gross GST revenue collec-
tion in March hit ₹2 lakh crore,
showing an 8.8% year-on-year
increase over ₹1.83 lakh crore
in the year-ago period.

After accounting for all re-
funds, the total net GST reve-
nue for the month stood at ₹1.77
lakh crore, reflecting an 8.2%
increase over ₹1.64 lakh crore
collected in the same month of
the previous year.

3 Market rises on hope of

4 Mid- and small-cap stocks
outperform large caps*

A closer look at the compo-
nents reveals that the gross do-
mestic revenue has gone up by
5.9% in March to ₹1.46 lakh
crore, which previously stood
at ₹1.38 lakh crore in March
2025. This domestic collection
consisted of ₹40,549 crore in

Govt says it allowed only partial pass-through of ATF price to prevent rise in domestic airfares

and consistent refunds bolster
the fiscal narrative, the persist-
ent rise in import GST coupled
with a softening in export re-
funds underscores a widening
trade gap,” said Saurabh Agar-
wal, Tax Partner, EY India.

There has been a significant
rise in the refund amount too,
with the total refund for March
amounting to ₹22,074 crore, up

the same month previous year.

Maharashtra accounted for
the highest collection with a to-
tal of ₹18,001crore in Post-Set-
tlement in this month.

only a partial pass-through to

in the country. As per oil mar-
keting companies, ATF for do-

or jet fuel — which con-
stitutes 40% of the total

ture of airlines — was
more than doubled, ris-

mestic airlines in Mumbai is



*ఈ చిత్రంలో తెలుపు రంగులో ఒక చిహ్నం ఉంది. ఇది ఒక పుస్తకాన్ని సూచిస్తుంది. పుస్తకంపై ఒక నీటి బిందువు కూడా ఉంది. ఈ చిహ్నం నీలం రంగు వృత్తాకారంలో ఉంది.*

₹98,247 per kilolitre, against the
full price of ₹1.95 lakh.

However, international or
charter operators will have to
bear full impact, with the price
of ATF in Delhi jumping 107%
to $1,690.81 per kilolitre. As per
the petroleum ministry, due to
the closure of the Strait of Hor-
muz and the extraordinary situ-

tion in global energy
markets, the price of
ATF for domestic mar-
kets was expected to
increase by over 100%
on April 1 for all users.
“In order to insulate
he domestic travel costs

from the substantial increase
in international prices, PSU oil
marketing companies of the
Ministry of Petroleum, in con-
sultation with Ministry of Civil
Aviation (MoCA), have passed
only a partial and staggered in-
crease of 25% (only ₹15/litre)
to the airlines. Foreign routes
will pay for the full increase in

ATF prices consistent with
what they pay in other parts of
the world," the MoPNG posted
on social media platform X.

The government also raised
commercial LPG rates by
₹195.50 per cylinder, along with
a ₹2 per litre hike in XP95, Pow-
er95, and Speed fuels. A 5-kg
mini cylinder has become cost-
lier by ₹51. A 19-kg commercial
LPG cylinder now costs
₹2,078.50 in Delhi. Rates were
last increased by ₹114.5 per 19-
kg cylinder on March 1.

Domestic cooking gas LPG
rates, last hiked by ₹60 per 14.2-
kg cylinder on March 7, remain
unchanged. It costs ₹913 per
14.2-kg cylinder in Delhi. The
Centre cited the ongoing war as
the reason, which has disrupt-
ed cargo movement through
the Strait of Hormuz, a vital
choke point that transports
40% of India’s crude oil im-
ports, over 50% of its LNG im-
ports, and 90% of its LPG.

## IndiGo raises
fuel surcharges
for second time

ENS ECONOMIC BUREAU @ New Delhi

AIRFARES are set to get pricier
as IndiGo has revised fuel
charges on domestic and inter-
national routes for all new
bookings made after 0001 hrs
on April 2, 2026. The move by
the country’s largest airline
comes after the oil marketing
companies (OMCs) revised avi-
ation turbine fuel (ATF) prices
on Wednesday.

It also comes despite the joint
secretary at the civil aviation
ministry Asangba Chuba Ao’s
remark that the government’s
decision on a limited increase
of jet fuel price ensures that
carriers’ domestic operational
costs remain manageable and
will not lead to additional fuel
surcharge.

IndiGo had last month intro-
duced a fuel surcharge be-
tween ₹399 and ₹2,300 for do-
mestic and international
flights as the ongoing conflict
in West Asia triggered a sharp
rise in energy prices.

The fresh revision, which is
now based on distance trav-
elled, takes the fuel surcharge
up to ₹950 (above 2000 km) for
domestic flights and up to
₹10,000 for flights to Europe
and the UK (other than Greece
and Turkey). It is expected that
other airlines will also revise
their fuel surcharge.

## ORACLE LAYS OFF THOUSANDS
GLOBALLY, 12,000 IN INDIA

PADMINI DHRUVARAJ@Bengaluru



*ఈ చిత్రంలో "ORACLE" అని రాసి ఉన్న ఒక పెద్ద భవనం కనిపిస్తుంది. ముందు భాగంలో కొన్ని కార్లు పార్క్ చేసి ఉన్నాయి.*

WHAT began as a routine
WEEKDAY morning quickly
turned unsettled for thou-
sands of employees at Ora-
cle, as termination emails
landed in their inboxes with-
out warning.

On March 31, staff across
multiple regions reported re-
ceiving notices as early as 6
am, informing them that
their roles had been eliminat-
ed with immediate effect.
“Today is your last working
day,” the email stated, citing
“organisational change” as
the reason. Access to internal
systems was revoked shortly
after, leaving many to absorb
the news in isolation.

As per multiple reports, the
US-based technology compa-
ny has begun a large-scale re-
structuring exercise that
could affect between 20,000
and 30,000 employees globally,
about 18% of its workforce of
162,000. India is believed to be
among the worst-hit regions,

with reports suggesting that
about 12,000 employees may
have been impacted.

The layoffs span several de-
partments, including engi-
neering, cloud operations,
sales and cybersecurity. While
the company has not officially
confirmed total number of job
cuts or detailed severance ar-
rangements, accounts shared
online show how abruptly the
changes took place.

The layoffs are a part of
Oracle’s ongoing restructur-
ing as it shifts resources to-
wards AI and cloud infra-

structure. The company has
announced plans to invest $50
billion in AI infrastructure.

The claim has not been in-
dependently verified, but it
has intensified discussion
around how major technolo-
gy firms are handling job
cuts during restructuring.

The scale of layoffs has
triggered reaction online,
particularly on X, Reddit and
LinkedIn, where current and
former employees have
shared their experiences. One
Reddit post that drew atten-
tion alleged a long-serving
Oracle employee battling can-
cer was dismissed via email
after 20 years with the com-
pany. “My dad has worked for
Oracle for 20 years, worked
for the same boss for 20
years,” the user wrote. “Not
even a phone call.”

Several other users also re-
ported receiving similar
emails. One commenter
wrote, “I was with the com-
pany for 29 years and got laid
off via email today.”

## Govt offers one-time duty relief for SEZ units

PUSHPITA DEY @ New Delhi

AMID global trade disruptions
due to West Asia crisis, the
Centre on Tuesday announced
a one-time relief measure for
eligible Special Economic Zone
(SEZ) units to allow them sell
manufactured goods in the do-
mestic tariff area (DTA) at con-
cessional Customs duty rates.

The scheme, introduced by
the Central Board of Indirect
Taxes and Customs (CBIC) in
line with the Union Budget
2026-27 announcements, will re-
main operational from April 1,



*ఈ చిత్రంలో నీలం రంగు నేపథ్యం ఉంది. ఇందులో ఎటువంటి వచనం, గ్రాఫిక్స్ లేదా ఇతర అంశాలు లేవు.*

2026 to March 31, 2027.

The relief applies to SEZ
units operational as of March
31, 2025. To avail this scheme,
the Centre has set eligibility
criteria like minimum 20% val-
ue addition and cap on domes-

tic sales linked to past export
performance. DTA sales have
been capped at 30% of past
peak export record in any of
three immediately preceding
financial years.

“By allowing SEZ units to

sell up to 30% of their export
turnover in domestic market,
the one-time relief window in-
troduces a calibrated and con-
trolled flexibility which will
ease pressure faced by existing
units in SEZ due to global trade
disruptions,” said sources from
finance ministry, adding that
the 30% cap on domestic sales
ensures SEZ units can’t shift
their focus away from exports.

Under the revised frame-
work, goods manufactured in
SEZs when sold domestically
will attract slightly lower basic
Customs duty (BCD).

## Tax relief for assets bought before Apr '17

DIPAK MONDAL @ New Delhi

THE government on Wednes-
day clarified that capital gains
from assets acquired before
April 1, 2017 will be exempted
from tax. The clarification
comes as fallout of the Tiger
Global ruling, in which the Su-
preme Court denied the US pri-
vate equity firm Mauritius tax
treaty benefits on capital gains
it made on the sale of unlisted

Flipkart shares in 2018.

The Central Board of Direct
Taxes (CBDT) has notified
changes in Rule 128 of the In-
come-tax Rules, 2026 to clarify
that capital gains accrued up to
1st April 2017 are protected
from subsequent changes in
tax regulations. The notifica-
tion further says that the tax
treatment of capital gains on
assets acquired prior to 1st
April 2017 is unlikely to be sub-

ject to renewed scrutiny by the
authorities, whether in terms
of substance or under the Gen-
eral Anti-Avoidance Rules
(GAAR).

Riaz Thingna, Partner, Grant
Thornton Bharat, says the clar-
ification is a result of the Tiger
Global ruling, which had cre-
ated uncertainty over the appli-
cability of grandfathering pro-
visions in respect of assets
acquired prior to April 1, 2017.

## GRSE hits new high
in turnover, declares
dividend of 129%

Kolkata: Garden Reach Shipbuilders
& Engineers Limited (GRSE),
sustaining its strong growth
momentum, has recorded the
highest annual turnover in its history
for FY26, amounting to ₹6,400 crore
(Provisional & Unaudited), as
against ₹5,076 crore in FY25. The
shipyard has declared an interim
dividend at 129% of paid-up share
capital against 89.5% in FY25. FY26
saw key milestones in naval
shipbuilding, with commissioning of
five vessels during the year, including
INS Himgiri, first Project 17A
Advanced Frigate, INS Ikshak, third
Survey Vessel (Large) and first three
Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow
Water Crafts (ASW-SWC)—INS
Arnala, INS Androth and INS Anjadip.
Marking a significant year in
execution and delivery, GRSE
delivered eight vessels to the Indian
Navy during FY26, comprising two
Project 17A (P17A) frigates, two
Survey Vessel Large (SVL) ships and
four Anti-Submarine Warfare
Shallow Water Crafts (ASW-SWC).

WITH the cap on banks taking
speculative positions on rupee
in overseas forward markets
failing to yield desired results,
the RBI has barred banks from
offering non-deliverable deriva-
tives (NDFs) in INR anymore to
anyone (resident or foreign).
NDFs are contracts where no
actual currency is exchanged.

In a new diktat, the RBI has
said banks can still offer nor-
mal (deliverable) forex deriva-
tives for genuine hedging (like
exporters/importers managing
currency risk), but users can-
not take opposite positions in
NDFs elsewhere to game the
system. If a forex derivative
contract is cancelled, the user
can’t rebook it again. This stops
people from cancelling and re-
entering trades to take advan-
tage of market movements.

Banks have been asked not to
enter such derivative contracts
with their own related entities
(group companies, affiliates,
etc.). These instructions come
into effect immediately, until
further review. Last week, the
RBI directed banks to limit their
net open position in rupee (NOP-
INR) in the onshore deliverable
market to $100 million at the end
of each business day, in a move
aimed at managing exchange
rate volatility. Despite the new-
ly-introduced cap on rupee bets,
the rupee fell like ninepins on
Monday to cross past the 95.20
for the first time in the second
half of the trade.

## India to play 10 T20Is in single month

Vishvanath, on the other
hand, put up a commanding
display against Bekzat Erge-
shov of Kyrgyzstan. The
Chennai boxer (50kg) won by
unanimous decision (5-0).
However, he will face a stiff
test in the next round as he'll
be up against No 1 seed
Sanzhar Tashkenbay of Kaza-
khstan. Tashkenbay is the
reigning world champ.

The Asian Boxing Champi-
onships continues to witness
high-intensity matchups as
top talents from across the
continent battle for
supremacy.

ENS @ Chennai

INDIA will play a three-match
T20I series in Zimbabwe in
July. The series is slated to be
crammed in a weekend in
Harare between July 23 and
July 26. India last visited the
African nation for a T20I bilat-
eral series in 2024. With Zimba-
bwe set to host part of the 50-
over World Cup in 2026, one
wonders if the Board of Con-
trol for Cricket in India (BCCI)
may consider picking a few of
their ace multi-format cricket-
ers to get them get familiar
with the conditions ahead of
the big event next year.

“Team India will head to
Zimbabwe for a three-match
T20I series in July 2026,” a
BCCI press release said. “The
Indian cricket team is sched-
uled to play three T20Is at the

Harare Sports Club, Harare.
The first T20I of the series will
be played on July 23, 2026.”

It means that the Indian
team, fresh from winning the
T20 World Cup at home, will
feature in as many as 10 T20Is
from the period between June
26 to July 26. And not to forget
the two-month long Indian Pre-
mier League (IPL) where al-

most all the India players are
expected to feature.

The Suryakumar-led outfit
will first travel to Ireland for a
pair of T20Is in Belfast on June
26 and June 28. Post that as-
signment — their first of the
next World Cup cycle — they
will take short flight to Eng-
land where they are scheduled
to play as many as five T20Is.
The series is part of their full
white-ball tour of England.

That tour culminates in
Southampton on July 11 before
the ODI series in Birmingham
starts on July 14. Four days af-
ter the final ODI, the team will
be featuring in their first of
T20Is in Harare. It’s interest-
ing to see that the team will be
engaged in this many T20Is at
a time when their next big
white-ball assignment is the
50-over World Cup.

*ఈ చిత్రం 'హిమాలయాలలో సాహిత్య స్వర్గం' (LITERARY HAVEN IN THE HIMALAYAS) అనే శీర్షికతో ఉన్న ఒక కోల్లెజ్. ఇందులో వివిధ దృశ్యాలు ఉన్నాయి: ఎగువ ఎడమ వైపున నీలి ఆకాశం కింద మంచుతో కప్పబడిన పర్వతాల దృశ్యం, ఎగువ కుడి వైపున ఎర్రటి పైకప్పు మరియు నీలిరంగు కిటికీలు కలిగిన తెల్లటి ఇంటి ఫోటో, దిగువ కుడి వైపున తెల్లటి గడ్డం ఉన్న ఒక వృద్ధుడి పెయింటింగ్, మరియు దిగువ ఎడమ వైపున 'హిమాలయ దృశ్యాలు' (Himalayan views) అని రాసి ఉన్న పర్వత ప్రాంతపు మ్యాప్ ఉన్నాయి. మధ్యలో ఉన్న ఒక చిన్న ఫోటోలో 'ఉత్తరాఖండ్' (Uttarakhand) అని రాసి ఉన్న ఒక చిన్న గుడి మరియు జెండాలు కనిపిస్తాయి. ఈ చిత్రంలో 'మెరా కుటి' (Meera Kuti) మరియు 'హిమాలయ దృశ్యాలు జహందిహార్' (Himalayan views from Jhandidhar) వంటి పేర్లు కూడా ఉన్నాయి.*



*ఈ చిత్రంలో రవీంద్రనాథ్ ఠాగూర్ విగ్రహం (Bust) ఉంది. విగ్రహం క్రింద రవీంద్రనాథ్ ఠాగూర్ జీవితం, రచనలు, అవార్డుల గురించి తెలిపే తెల్లటి ఫలకం ఉంది. ఫలకంపై "గुरूदेव", "రవీంద్రనాథ్ ఠాగూర్" అని వ్రాసి ఉంది. ఫలకంపై "జననం: 7 మే 1861", "మరణం: 7 ఆగస్టు 1941" అని రాసి ఉంది.*

ANURAG MALLICK & PRIYA GANAPATHY

Baksh served the British, trans-

at tourist spots.”

India’s newest museum opens its
doors in Gujarat, honouring the ruler
who carried Jainism to the world

EXPRESS NEWS SERVICE

On the auspicious occasion of
Mahavir Jayanti, Prime Minis-
ter Narendra Modi inaugurated
the *Samrat Samprati Museum*,
known in Gujarati as the *Sam-*
*rat Samprati Sangrahalaya*, on the
serene Koba Tirth campus in Gan-
dhinagar. To visit it is to step inside
two and a half millennia of living
faith. Koba Tirth, formally the *Shri*
*Mahavir Jain Aradhana Kendra*, al-
ready draws pilgrims from across
India. The new museum transforms
it into something broader still: a des-
tination for travellers with even a
passing curiosity about South Asian
history, philosophy or the remark-
able civilisation that grew up along-
side and sometimes in conversation
with the Mauryan empire.

Acharya Padmasagar Surishwar-
ji, a Jain monk conceived the mu-
seum and spent years gathering the
rare artefacts now assembled within
its walls. The collection he has be-
queathed to posterity numbers more
than 2,000 objects, arranged chron-
ologically across seven wings. Visi-
tors enter through an introduction
to the two foundational tenets of
Jainism: ahimsa, the principle of
non-violence and aparigraha, non-
possessiveness.

Pride of place among the early
galleries belongs to artefacts asso-
ciated with the 24 Tirthankaras. A
highlight is a Jina Matruka Patta

ologically across seven wings. Visi-
tors enter through an introduction
to the two foundational tenets of
Jainism: ahimsa, the principle of
non-violence and aparigraha, non-
possessiveness.

## WITNESS KONYAK NAGA TRIBE'S
UNIQUE FESTIVAL IN NAGALAND



*ఈ చిత్రంలో సాంప్రదాయ గిరిజన దుస్తులు ధరించిన ముగ్గురు మహిళలు కనిపిస్తున్నారు. వారు నలుపు రంగు దుస్తులు ధరించి, తెల్లటి ఈకల వంటి అలంకరణలు మరియు ఎరుపు, పసుపు రంగు పూసల హారాలను ధరించారు. ముందున్న మహిళ ఒక పొడవైన చెక్క కర్రను పట్టుకుని ఉంది. వారి దుస్తులలో రంగురంగుల అంచు ఉన్న స్కర్టులు ఉన్నాయి. నేపథ్యం అస్పష్టంగా ఉంది, ఇది బహిరంగ ప్రదేశం లేదా వేడుకను సూచిస్తుంది.*

The Aoleang Festival 2026 is Nagaland's major spring harvest festival celebrated in

Nagaland's major spring
harvest festival celebrated in
Mon in the first week of April. It
marks the Konyak New Year with
traditional dances with real spears
and guns, songs, rice beer, tattooed
elders, hornbill headdresses and
log drum performances inside
decorated morungs — all while the
mist hangs over the Patkai hills at
dawn. Participants often visit the
Angh (village chief) house in
Longwa, which straddles the
India-Myanmar border.



*ఈ చిత్రం ఒక పండుగ లేదా మతపరమైన ఊరేగింపును వర్ణిస్తుంది. చిత్ర మధ్యలో, ఎరుపు మరియు పసుపు పూలతో అలంకరించబడిన ఒక బంగారు రంగు విగ్రహం లేదా విగ్రహం ఉంది. ఈ విగ్రహాన్ని కొందరు వ్యక్తులు మోస్తున్నారు. చుట్టూ ఉన్న ప్రజలు పసుపు రంగు చొక్కాలు మరియు టోపీలు ధరించి ఉన్నారు, ఇది ఒక సామూహిక కార్యక్రమాన్ని సూచిస్తుంది. నేపథ్యంలో చాలా మంది ప్రజలు గుమిగూడి ఉన్నారు, ఇది ఒక పెద్ద వేడుకను సూచిస్తుంది.*

## WATCH A DIVINE WEDDING UNFOLD
AT MADURAI'S CHITHIRAI FESTIVAL

This grand month-long festival is celebrated in April,



*I 🔵 🔴 ⚪ 🟡 ⚪*

■ focusing on the marriage of
Meenakshi Amman and
Sundareswarar and the immersion
of Kallazhagar in the Vaigai River.
The first 15 days will see the
coronation of Meenakshi Amman,
digvijayam and thirukalyanam (the
marriage of Shiva and Parvati).
The last day, called the *urchava*
*saatru murai*, brings the complete
Kallazhagar festival to a
ceremonial conclusion.
